_comment: GENERATED by `python3 -m edge_workbench.prepare`. Do not edit:
re-run it. This is what the build reads instead of the
tutorial, so that a build depends on files in this repository
and not on which branch a sibling checkout happens to be on.
`source.sha` is the commit the tutorial was read at. A gate
compares it against the tutorial's head to tell you when the
tutorial has moved and this needs re-running.
`gaps` lists what the tutorial does not state in a form this
step can read. Those are the model-assisted half's input; an
empty list means the tutorial said everything itself.

meanings.E01: The most recently pushed alternative (the deepest one) is the next candidate row to try, which is what makes the search depth-first.
meanings.E02: The stamp's depth says how far down the search tree the chosen row sits, and so how far back the path must be cut.
meanings.E03: The row now being explored is consumed, so the stack keeps only the untried sibling alternatives.
meanings.E04: Which path entries were chosen at a depth shallower than the popped one: the prefix backtracking keeps.
meanings.E05: Backtracking discards every path entry at or below the new choice's depth, because those rows belong to abandoned branches.
meanings.E06: The row just popped becomes the path's entry for the new depth.
meanings.E07: The path for the next step is the surviving prefix of the old path plus the newly chosen row.
meanings.E08: The rows on the path are the partial solution built so far.
meanings.E09: A column counts as covered once some row already on the path contains it.
meanings.E10: The columns still needing exactly one cover are the ones the path has not yet covered.
meanings.E11: A row that shares a column with the path can never join this partial solution, since that column would be covered twice.
meanings.E12: The rows that can still legally extend the partial solution are those that are neither in conflict nor already chosen.
meanings.E13: The path is an exact cover exactly when no column is left uncovered.
meanings.E14: When the path is an exact cover, its rows are reported as a solution.
meanings.E15: Each column's degree is the number of still-eligible rows that could cover it, which measures how constrained it is.
meanings.E16: Only uncovered columns keep their degree, so columns the path already covers cannot be picked to branch on.
meanings.E17: Branching on the most constrained uncovered column is Knuth's minimum-degree heuristic, and it keeps the search tree small.
meanings.E18: The candidates are the eligible rows that could cover the chosen column, and exactly one of them must be in any solution.
meanings.E19: Sibling alternatives are stamped one level deeper than the current choice, so they are explored before older, shallower alternatives.
meanings.E20: The untried alternatives from every level stay on the stack, with the newest siblings on top, so backtracking can resume from them.

tensorNotes.A: The static Boolean input matrix: entry (r, c) is True when row r covers column c.
tensorNotes.S: The stack of alternative choices; each entry at row r holds that row's depth stamp.
tensorNotes.Path: The rows chosen so far, each mapped to the depth at which it was selected.
tensorNotes.SelRow: The set of rows currently on the path.
tensorNotes.CovCol: The set of columns covered by the rows on the path.
tensorNotes.ConflictRow: Rows that overlap with columns the path already covers.
tensorNotes.ActiveRow: The rows still eligible for selection.
tensorNotes.Success: Flag that is True when every column is covered.
tensorNotes.RowCounts: The cover degree of each column.
tensorNotes.PickedCol: The column chosen to cover next.
tensorNotes.Candidates: The active rows that cover the chosen column.
tensorNotes.Keep: Path entries shallower than the popped depth, the ones backtracking keeps

quotes.E01: pops the deepest choice (largest stamp) to explore
quotes.E04: We truncate any choices made at depths
quotes.E05: truncates the active path to match the backtrack depth
quotes.E08: the set of rows currently in the path
quotes.E09: the set of columns covered by the path
quotes.E11: rows that overlap with columns already covered by the path
quotes.E12: the remaining rows eligible for selection
quotes.E13: flag indicating whether all columns are covered
quotes.E14: If no active columns remain, we write the solution
quotes.E15: we count covering active rows for each active column
quotes.E16: we count covering active rows for each active column
quotes.E17: pick the column with the minimum count
quotes.E18: the active rows covering the chosen column
quotes.E19: push its covering active rows onto the stack with the new depth
